answer.rationale: Binding constraints: the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and the contract lapses in 14 days. That combination makes a primary-vendor switch the wrong single move this cycle even though memory_c2 records a sharp unit-cost win from the low-cost vendor  irst even any smooth onboarding takes qualification and first-article time we do not have; a slipped first shipment converts a cost saving into a delivery failure. defer_decision (memory_c5) worked for a non-critical service on month-to-month terms; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferral means falling out of contract on a critical input, not preserving optionality. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right structural fix for single-point-of-failure risk and should be the candidate for the next review, but it adds cost rather than cutting it and does not answer the 18% mandate. That leaves negotiating the incumbent renewal: memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, and memory_c6 says a longer term unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope, while memory_c1 says renewal avoids migration work entirely  irst cost relief with no delivery risk added. I spent the single verification pull on memory_c4 because it is the load-bearing claim for this action and the one whose magnitude decides feasibility: if the archived record shows the recovery was only a few points, negotiation alone cannot reach 18% and I need to stack a multi-year volume commitment or return to finance and contest the target. I did not verify memory_c2 because no plausible content in it would make a 14-day vendor migration safe against a zero-buffer line. Uncertainty I am not resolving: none of these memories records the counterfactual cost, whether the recorded conditions match today's volume and market, or whether the incumbent's leverage has shifted now that they know we are 14 days out  irst that timing may cut against us in a way memory_c4 never faced. Downstream value risk: an 18% cut pursued hard tends to be paid for somewhere off the invoice  irst tolerance drift, quality escapes, deprioritized allocation, or a longer commitment that removes our freedom to dual-source later. I will hold scope and quality terms fixed in writing, cap the term so the second-source option stays live for the next review, and treat any concession that trades spec or allocation priority for headline price as a decline rather than a win.
